title: US Mortgage Rates Climb Above 7 Percent for First Time in 20 Months
subtitle: Rising borrowing costs and economic uncertainty create new challenges for American homebuyers.

summary.en: US mortgage rates have officially crossed the 7% threshold for the first time since January 2025. This increase is driven by Federal Reserve interest rate hikes intended to fight high inflation. The rising costs are putting further pressure on an already slow housing market. Many potential buyers are finding it harder to afford homes as monthly payments become more expensive. Experts suggest these economic challenges could play a significant role in upcoming political discussions.
summary.zh: 美國房貸利率自二零二五年一月以來，正式突破百分之七的門檻。此次上升是由聯準會為對抗高通膨而採取的升息措施所推動。不斷攀升的成本對原本就已低迷的房地產市場造成了進一步壓力。隨著每月還款額變得更加昂貴，許多潛在買家發現購屋變得更加困難。專家認為，這些經濟挑戰可能會在未來的政治討論中扮演重要角色。

paragraphs.en: For the first time in 20 months, mortgage rates in the United States have climbed above 7%. According to Freddie Mac, a federal lender, the average 30-year fixed-rate mortgage reached 7.03% on Thursday. This development marks a difficult turn for a housing market that has already struggled with years of high costs and a low supply of available homes.
paragraphs.zh: 美國的房貸利率二十個月以來首次攀升至百分之七以上。根據聯邦貸款機構房地美 (Freddie Mac) 的數據，週四平均三十年期固定房貸利率達到百分之七點零三。這項發展對房地產市場而言是一個艱難的轉折，該市場早已深受多年來的高成本與房屋供給短缺所苦。

paragraphs.en: This increase follows a recent decision by the US Federal Reserve to raise its benchmark interest rate by a quarter of a percentage point. This was the first time the central bank has increased rates this year. The Federal Reserve is taking these steps to combat high inflation, which continues to affect the cost of living for many Americans. According to NPR News, many policymakers have indicated that they might raise rates at least one more time before the end of 2026 as they work to bring inflation under control.
paragraphs.zh: 此次利率上升，源於美國聯邦準備理事會 (Federal Reserve) 近期決定將基準利率調升四分之一個百分點。這是該央行今年首次升息。聯準會採取這些措施是為了對抗高通貨膨脹，而通膨持續影響著許多美國人的生活成本。根據美國國家公共廣播電台 (NPR) 報導，許多決策官員已暗示，為了控制通膨，他們在二零二六年年底前可能至少還會再升息一次。

paragraphs.en: Experts note that the rise in mortgage rates is closely linked to the 10-year Treasury note, which has seen its value change rapidly over the summer. Investors are worried about both the high levels of inflation and the size of the national debt. As a result, the 10-year Treasury yield recently reached its highest level since July 2007. The Guardian Business reports that these rising yields directly influence the cost of borrowing for home loans, making it more expensive for people to finance a property.
paragraphs.zh: 專家指出，房貸利率的上升與十年期公債殖利率密切相關，後者在夏季期間價值波動劇烈。投資人擔憂高通膨與國家債務規模。結果，十年期公債殖利率近期創下二零零七年七月以來的新高。衛報商業版 (The Guardian Business) 報導稱，這些殖利率的上升直接影響了房屋貸款的借貸成本，使得民眾購屋的融資負擔變得更加沉重。

paragraphs.en: Economic events outside of the United States are also playing a significant role. Since the start of the war between the US and Iran in late February, energy prices have risen sharply. Brent crude oil, an international benchmark for oil prices, recently topped $105 per barrel. This conflict has caused instability in the bond markets and increased concerns about long-term inflation, which in turn pushes mortgage rates higher.
paragraphs.zh: 美國境外的經濟事件也扮演了重要角色。自二月底美國與伊朗爆發戰爭以來，能源價格急劇上漲。作為國際油價基準的布蘭特原油，近期每桶價格突破一百零五美元。這場衝突導致債券市場不穩定，並加劇了對長期通膨的擔憂，進而推高了房貸利率。

paragraphs.en: For many Americans, the dream of owning a home is becoming increasingly difficult to reach. Anthony Smith, a senior economist at Realtor.com, explained that the housing market has been in a slowdown for a long time. Data from the National Association of Realtors shows that existing home sales fell by 2% in August compared to the previous month. With the median sale price for an existing home at approximately $429,000, even a small increase in mortgage rates can add hundreds of dollars to a monthly payment. Over the life of a 30-year loan, these costs can add up to tens of thousands of dollars.
paragraphs.zh: 對許多美國人來說，擁有房屋的夢想變得越來越難以實現。房地產網站 Realtor.com 的資深經濟學家安東尼·史密斯 (Anthony Smith) 解釋說，房地產市場長期以來一直處於低迷狀態。美國全國房地產經紀人協會 (National Association of Realtors) 的數據顯示，八月份成屋銷售量較前一個月下降了百分之二。由於成屋銷售中位價約為四十二萬九千美元，即使房貸利率微幅上升，每月還款額也會增加數百美元。在三十年貸款期間，這些成本累計起來可能高達數萬美元。

paragraphs.en: While some housing researchers had hoped that 2026 would offer relief for buyers, those expectations have faded. Mortgage rates had briefly fallen below 6% in February, but they have since moved upward. Smith noted that the 7% level is both a mathematical reality and a psychological barrier for many people. It arrives at a time of year when buyers usually expect to have more power in the market, but the current economic environment has kept the market stagnant instead.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管一些房地產研究人員曾寄望二零二六年能為買家帶來緩解，但這些期望已經破滅。房貸利率曾在二月份短暫跌破百分之六，但隨後便一路走高。史密斯指出，百分之七的利率水準對許多人而言，既是數學上的現實，也是心理上的障礙。此時正值買家通常預期在市場上擁有更多議價能力的季節，但當前的經濟環境卻使市場持續停滯。

paragraphs.en: These financial pressures are also becoming a topic of political debate. With midterm elections approaching in November, the economy is a major concern for voters. A recent CNN poll conducted by SSRS found that two-thirds of registered voters consider the economy to be extremely important to their vote. The poll also showed that nearly three-quarters of Americans disapprove of how Donald Trump has handled the economy, suggesting that the frustration over housing costs and inflation could influence the upcoming elections.
paragraphs.zh: 這些財務壓力也正成為政治辯論的話題。隨著十一月期中選舉臨近，經濟成為選民極為關切的議題。美國有線電視新聞網 (CNN) 近期委託 SSRS 進行的一項民調發現，三分之二的登記選民認為經濟對他們的投票意向至關重要。民調也顯示，近四分之三的美國人不認同川普 (Donald Trump) 對經濟的處理方式，這顯示出對房價與通膨的挫折感可能會影響即將到來的選舉。

paragraphs.en: As the year continues, the outlook for the housing market remains uncertain. While Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent announced that the government would triple its buyback of government debt, market yields have continued to rise. Investors are now preparing for the possibility of further rate hikes from the Federal Reserve. For now, homebuyers and sellers alike are waiting to see if the market will find stability or if the current trend of high costs and low activity will continue into the future.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著今年持續進行，房地產市場的前景依然不明朗。儘管財政部長史考特·貝森特 (Scott Bessent) 宣布政府將擴大三倍的政府債務回購規模，但市場殖利率仍持續攀升。投資人目前正為聯準會可能進一步升息做準備。目前，購屋者與賣方都在觀望市場是否會恢復穩定，或者高成本與低交易量的現狀是否會持續到未來。

keyTerms.definitionEn: A change in the direction or nature of a situation.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作動詞（轉彎），這裡作名詞表示局勢的變化。文中：This development marks a difficult turn for a housing market that has already struggled with years of high costs and a low supply of available homes.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To result in a particular total amount.
keyTerms.noteZh: 由動詞與介系詞組成，意思非字面相加，指累積的總額。文中：Over the life of a 30-year loan, these costs can add up to tens of thousands of dollars.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Not moving or making progress; inactive.
keyTerms.noteZh: 原意指水流不通，這裡形容市場缺乏活力與交易。文中：It arrives at a time of year when buyers usually expect to have more power in the market, but the current economic environment has kept the market stagnant instead.

quiz.question: What is the primary reason mentioned for the recent increase in mortgage rates according to the third paragraph?

options.A: A decrease in the national debt
options.B: The rising yield of the 10-year Treasury note
options.C: A sudden drop in the demand for new homes
options.D: The government's decision to stop buying back debt

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第三段，專家指出抵押貸款利率的上升與 10 年期國債（10-year Treasury note）密切相關，且該國債殖利率達到 2007 年以來的高點，這直接影響了房屋貸款的借貸成本。選項 A 錯誤，因為文章提到的是國債規模大導致投資者擔憂；選項 C 雖然提到房屋市場低迷，但並非解釋利率上升的直接原因；選項 D 則與最後一段提到的政府回購債務內容混淆，且與第三段提到的國債殖利率無關。

quiz.question: Based on the information provided, what can be inferred about the impact of the current economic climate on homebuyers?

options.A: Buyers have more bargaining power because it is the time of year when they usually expect it
options.B: The rise in rates has made homeownership significantly more expensive over the long term
options.C: Most Americans are choosing to wait until 2026 to buy homes because rates are expected to drop
options.D: The housing market is currently experiencing a surge in sales due to low supply

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據第五段，即使利率微幅上升，也會增加每月還款額，且在 30 年的貸款期限內，總成本會增加數萬美元，這顯示長期持有成本大幅增加。選項 A 錯誤，第六段明確指出儘管季節性因素通常有利於買家，但目前的經濟環境使市場處於停滯狀態；選項 C 錯誤，文中提到對 2026 年的緩解期待已經破滅；選項 D 錯誤，第五段數據顯示房屋銷售量實際上是下降的。

quiz.question: In the sixth paragraph, what does the author mean by describing the 7% mortgage rate as a 'psychological barrier'?

options.A: It is a level that causes people to feel discouraged or hesitant about buying a home
options.B: It is a limit set by the government that cannot be legally exceeded
options.C: It is a mathematical error that analysts are trying to correct
options.D: It is a target that the Federal Reserve wants all banks to reach

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。在此語境中，「psychological barrier」（心理障礙）指的是一個特定的數據點（7%），它不僅僅是一個數學數字，更會影響人們的信心與決策，讓潛在買家感到壓力而卻步。選項 B 錯誤，這不是法律限制；選項 C 錯誤，文中並未提到這是數學錯誤；選項 D 錯誤，這並非聯準會的目標，而是市場壓力下的結果。

quiz.question: What is the central theme of the article?

options.A: The history of the US Federal Reserve's interest rate policies
options.B: The political impact of the upcoming midterm elections on oil prices
options.C: The challenges facing the US housing market due to rising rates and economic instability
options.D: The reasons why investors are choosing to buy government debt instead of homes

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。整篇文章從抵押貸款利率突破 7% 開始，探討了聯準會政策、國債殖利率、國際衝突及經濟壓力如何共同導致房屋市場陷入停滯，並增加了美國人購屋的困難度，這是全文的核心主旨。選項 A 僅是部分內容；選項 B 僅在最後一段簡短提及；選項 D 並非文章討論的重點，文章主要聚焦於購屋者的困境。
